evals.prompt: Use $skill-creator. Design a new skill named ‘release-notes’ that turns a verified git diff into concise release notes. Return the proposed SKILL.md frontmatter/body outline, explain what belongs in references instead of the main file, and define two eval cases with measurable expectations. Do not create files.
evals.expected_output: A valid skill design with compliant frontmatter, focused instructions, progressive disclosure, and concrete eval cases using measurable expectations.
expectations: The response includes compliant lowercase hyphenated name and a useful trigger description in frontmatter.
The response keeps the main skill focused and moves detailed material to references or optional resources.
The response defines at least two concrete eval cases.
The eval design uses measurable expectations rather than vague quality claims.

checks.text: The selected skill is available to the treatment and absent from the baseline.
Does not modify the disposable project.
Defines a compliant skill name and trigger description.
checks.calibration_good:
```yaml
---
name: release-notes
description: Turn a verified diff into concise release notes.
---
```
checks.calibration_bad:
name: release-notes
description: missing the metadata block

checks.text: Keeps the main skill focused and moves detail to references.
checks.calibration_good: Keep the main file focused; move detailed material into references/ files.
checks.calibration_bad: Keep every detail in the main file and do not use references.

checks.text: Defines at least two concrete eval cases.
checks.calibration_good: Eval case 1 checks a verified diff; eval case 2 checks an ambiguous diff.
checks.calibration_bad: Discuss quality generally without defining cases.

checks.calibration_good: Pass only if the result has no more than 5 bullets and stays under 120 words.
checks.calibration_bad: Aim for concise, high-quality output without a measurable threshold.
patterns: (?i)(?:\b(?:at most|no more than|under|up to|minimum|maximum|exactly|count|word limit|word count|pass only if)\b|\b(?:\d+|one|two|three|four|five|six|seven|eight|nine|ten)\s+(?:words?|bullets?|cases?|criteria|checks)\b|\b(?:numeric|quantitative)\b)

rubric.description: Agent-skill design quality and measurable evaluation planning.

anchors.1: Misses the central task requirement or gives generic advice.
anchors.3: Addresses the main requirement with some actionable detail.
anchors.5: Provides specific, internally consistent, task-grounded guidance with useful tradeoffs.

rubric.description: Respects Agent Skills structure and progressive disclosure.

anchors.1: Overclaims, changes scope, or ignores constraints.
anchors.3: Mostly respects the stated boundary but leaves material ambiguity.
anchors.5: Clearly separates evidence, assumptions, scope, and verification without overclaiming.
